messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager fired: GPU memory pressure on pool 'inference-1' (eu-west-1). 22/48 GPUs > 92% vmem, repeated cudaMallocFailed attempts, kernel OOM hints. Auto-shedder triggered.

pagerduty: PagerDuty alert: HIGH severity - 'gpu_memory_pressure_inference-1' (service: gpu-inference-eu). Triggered at 2025-11-03T09:12:01Z.

Rafi: acked via PD :white_check_mark: I'm on it, starting quick triage. Anyone running recent model rollout to that pool?

Elena: I see a pattern of one workload leaking KV cache entries in logs. Repeats of: `CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED` and `cudaMemcpyAsync failed`. grabbing dmesg tail.

Elena: ```
[ 3487.123456] NVRM: GPU 0: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 79, pid=8421, name=python, Ch 00000052, Reason: Page allocation failure
[ 3487.123459] NVRM: GPU 0: GPU memory: 0x7f8a3c0000 -> allocation failed
```

Jordan: good catch. Rafi, can you `ssh` into one of the affected hosts and run `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION` and `ps` to find the offender? We'll consider draining the pool and rerouting to fallback quantized variants.

Rafi: on host inference-1-node-14 now. nvidia-smi:```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.89.02    Driver Version: 525.89.02    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0   A100-SXM4-40G    Off        | 00000000:AF:00.0 Off | N/A                  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                       GPU Memory |
|  GPU   PID   Type   Process name                             Usage        |
|    0  8421   C+G    python /app/runner.py                        39240MiB |
|    0  9002   C      python /app/workers/async_infer.py            1024MiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Looks like pid 8421 is eating 39GB. It's a long-running batch job from team-search.

Rafi: `top` shows the process hasn't crashed but is steadily growing memory. I can kill it, but that will drop in-flight requests. Jordan, what's the mitigation policy?

Jordan: Priority is to avoid widespread timeouts. Do a graceful drain of the node and move live traffic to fallback routes. Commands:```
redwoodctl pool drain inference-1 --hosts inference-1-node-14 --grace 30
redwoodctl route update --pool inference-1 --fallback-model gpt-medium-quant --weight 30
```
Execute drain and start reroute. Notify customers after initial stabilization.

incident-bot: Started drain job inference-1-node-14 (grace 30s). Routing policy update queued.

Maya: I'm updating routing now. Pushing fallback weight to 40% for quick relief.

Rafi: killed pid 8421 gracefully (SIGTERM), waited 25s, then SIGKILL after no exit. Node freed ~38GB. `nvidia-smi` now shows normal usage: 6GB for system + other small procs.

Elena: I'm seeing fewer `cudaMalloc` errors in the logs post-kill. We're seeing some client errors: a spike of 502/504s from a small subset of customers hitting model `gpt-medium` in eu-west-1 around 09:10-09:18. Cartography shows ~2% of requests got retried/failed, p50->p95 latency jump to 1.2s->5.6s.

Rafi: Confirmed. I opened an internal incident ticket (INC-2025-341) and flagged two affected customers in the dashboard (cust_198, cust_712). Support pinged them with ETA.

Jordan: Good. We'll keep fallback in place for 15m and monitor. Maya, can you escalate to eng-runtime to review the batch job that leaked KV cache? Tagging @Elena and add the process logs.

Maya: Escalated to #eng-runtime, pinging @runtime-oncall. Also creating a short reproduction ticket with the stack trace and the `python` command line.

Elena: For postmortem - note that autoscaling and auto-shedder recovered capacity but took ~90s to fully re-balance; that window caused the client-visible errors. Suggest: tune auto-shedder thresholds or faster fallback routing.

Rafi: quick checkpoint: node back to healthy, routing fallback weight 40%, metrics trending down. No further PD alerts in the last 6 minutes.

pagerduty: Acknowledgement: Alert acknowledged by Rafi at 2025-11-03T09:16:45Z. No further escalations required.

Jordan: I'm handing off to Maya (I need to step out). Watch the error rate for next 30m, if >1% fail reopen PD. Leaving runbook actions: 1) add an exclusion rule for batch workers to cap GPU mem; 2) review recent deploys; 3) follow-up postmortem.

Maya: Taking over handoff. I'll keep a watch and coordinate postmortem write-up. Noting the remediation: killed leaking process, drained host, adjusted routing to quantized fallback.

Elena: quick log snippet for postmortem:```
2025-11-03T09:09:58Z ERROR cudaMalloc failed: out of memory, requested 256MB
2025-11-03T09:10:15Z WARN eviction initiated for kvcache key=ctx:abc123 size=512MB
2025-11-03T09:11:01Z INFO auto-shedder rerouted 12% traffic to fallback
```

Rafi: Closing the PD incident now. I'll attach heap samples and process cmdline to INC-2025-341.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident closed by Rafi at 2025-11-03T09:25:20Z.

Maya: All stable here. We'll draft a postmortem and recommended follow-ups: memory caps for batch jobs, tighter shedder thresholds, add alert to detect long-running single-proc dominant GPU usage.

Elena: Thanks team. I'll start the postmortem draft and ping product for customer comms.

Maya: handing off to on-call rotation notes: no active page now. If error rate creeps up, reopen PD.

Jordan: back briefly — thanks, good job.

Maya: marking thread resolved, will add link to postmortem when done.
